Sections covered: Appetizers, Soup, Salads, Wraps, Entrees, Meza Platter, Traditional Dishes, Sides and Extras, Desserts, Beverages, Beer, Glass of Wine, Bottles of Wine - matches the full section list shown on the Wix menu tabs, no core section appears missing.

name: Domo Kitchen
notes: Menu is 7 photographed pages of the restaurant's own printed laminated menu, posted on their own site's '#menu' section (no separate menu page/PDF; a #contactform/#hours single-pager). Photo files are dated 2018 (HTTP Last-Modified), so cross-checked every item against allmenus.com's structured schema.org JSON-LD (107 items) which is independently derived. The two agreed exactly on the large majority of items (a la carte Starters, Soups, Specialties, Shrimp & Fish, Beef, Chicken, Pork, most Noodles/Veggies/Salads), which resolved a camera-tilt pairing ambiguity on the Starters page (item name and price rows were offset by one visual row; sequential item-order-to-price-order pairing was confirmed correct by matching 'Domo Famous Beef Short Ribs'=$12.95 and 'Steamed Edamame'=$3.00 on both sources). Where the two sources disagreed, the printed photo (first-party) was used and allmenus was treated as the stale one: the entire Lunch section and two salads (House Salad, Sunomono Salad) were a uniform $1.00 higher on the photo than on allmenus, and Veggie Lo Mein / one Fried Rice line / one 'Grill Salmon' line each had one differing duplicate entry on allmenus that the photo's single value resolved. Two items (Crab Salad, Salmon Skin Salad) are struck through with pen on the physical menu photo and were dropped as discontinued. A few faint handwritten price annotations elsewhere (near Miso Soup, Bottle Water/Iced Tea, Beers header, Cashew/Lemon Chicken) could not be reliably attributed to a specific item and were ignored in favor of the printed price. Sections covered: Starters, Soups, Salads, Domo Kitchen Specialties, Shrimp & Fish, Noodles, Fried Rice, Veggies, Beverages, Beers, Wine, Sake, Lunch, Beef, Chicken, Pork - this is every section shown across all 7 official menu photos. Web search summaries describe the restaurant as also serving sushi rolls/nigiri/hand rolls, but no rolls/sushi section appears on the restaurant's own printed menu (all 7 pages read) nor on the allmenus listing, so none is included; this may mean rolls are on a separate insert not photographed, not that no such items exist.

name: Old Town Saloon
notes: not_found. this is a dive bar / pool hall (Yelp category 'Pool Halls'; three pool tables, jukebox), not a restaurant. Its California ABC liquor license is explicitly 'ON SALE GENERAL PUBLIC PREMISE/BAR COCKTAILS ONLY - NO FOOD'. No working restaurant-owned website exists: the work list has no website, oldtownsaloonsd.wix.com/bars 404s, and oldtownsaloon.net (found via search) is a same-named but DIFFERENT dive bar in Naples, FL (page title: 'Old Town Saloon - Must-Try Dive Bar in Naples, FL') - not used. Checked Facebook page, Tripadvisor, yellowpages, and a happy-hour aggregator: only per-drink happy hour specials appear ($2-$20 drinks, $2 jello shots, $2 Natty Lights during Mon-Fri 10:30am-6pm happy hour) and a vague mention of 'selected Happy Hour food' with no items or prices given anywhere. No per-item priced food or drink menu was found on any source, consistent with the no-food license. Recording as not_found per the drink-only dive bar rule.

name: cardellino
notes: Restaurant's own Squarespace site, server-rendered plain HTML (page title 'Dinner Menu | Cardellino Mission Hills'). Prices on this site are printed as bare integers with no '$' character (e.g. 'MEATBALLS ... 19'), confirmed to be prices by their position, formatting, and range immediately after every dish description across every section - the '$' was added when recording to match the required price format, no value was computed or altered. Every dinner-menu item's price appears twice in the raw HTML (a responsive-layout duplicate) - de-duplicated by name. Two items (Ahi Tuna Tartare, Filet Mignon Carpaccio) carry a '*' on the menu (raw/undercooked disclaimer); the '*' was dropped from the price field and noted in the description instead, price itself unchanged. Covered: Antipasti, Pasta, Secondi, Contorni (from /dinner), Dessert + Daily Scoop + Dopo Cena (after-dinner drinks) + Amaro (from /dessert), Cocktails + Wine by the Glass (from /drinks). Deliberately excluded: the /drinks page's 'Wines by the Bottle' list (Rosé+Bubbles, Whites, Large Format, Reserve List, Reds - dozens of bottles from $37 to $690), treated as an adjunct back-of-house wine reference rather than a core menu section, consistent with excluding bottle-service/back-bar lists. Also excluded the /happy-hour page, which is only a text blurb ('all wine bottles half off Tuesday'), not an itemized menu. /menu redirects to /dinner; the site has no lunch or brunch page.

name: Albert's Mexican Food
notes: This chain has several San Diego-area locations with separate menu pages (/menu/el-cajon, /menu/la-mesa, /menu/lakeside); used /menu/la-mesa specifically to match this record's address (8038 La Mesa Blvd, La Mesa, CA 91942). Prices are server-rendered plain text on the restaurant's own domain (ordersave.com-powered ordering widget embedded in the page). Ran the markup-divisor test: dividing all 55 unique prices by 1.10 lands the large majority within a cent of a clean value, a real signal worth flagging. However, this was NOT treated as proof of a delivery markup requiring a lower 'true' price, for two reasons: (1) an independent source, menupages.com, shows the SAME items 10-18% HIGHER than this site (e.g. Beef Chimichanga a la carte $15.34 here vs $17.85 on menupages; Carne Asada Chimichanga $17.54 vs $19.25) - if this site were inflated above the real dine-in price, an independent source should show something LOWER, not higher; (2) a much older SinglePlatform listing for this restaurant shows the same items at roughly half this site's prices (Chimichanga $7.95), which is textbook staleness (SinglePlatform is known stale-by-default) and confirms prices have genuinely risen over time - this site's numbers sit in a plausible place on that trend, not off of it. So the 1.10 pattern was judged most likely an artifact of the restaurant's own combo-pricing structure rather than an imposed online-ordering surcharge, and this site's own prices were used as-is (never divided/constructed). Confidence set to medium rather than high because that 1.10 pattern is still unexplained and no printed/photographed in-store menu could be found to settle it outright (Yelp's menu tab is barred, no dated menu photo was located). Sections covered (all 22 on the page): Combination Plates, Burritos, Chimichanga, Tacos, Big Rolled Tacos, Small Rolled Tacos, Tortas, Tostadas, Quesadillas, Enchiladas, Bowls, Breakfast Plates, Breakfast Burritos, Burger & Fries, Alberts Wrap, Salads, Soups, Nachos & Fries, Kids Meal, A La Carte, Extra (add-ons), Beverages. Two items ('Chimichanga Plate Combo', "Albert's Wraps") were marked with a '+' on the site meaning a starting/from price; the '+' was dropped from the price field (kept regex-valid) and noted in the description instead, price value itself unchanged. A handful of item descriptions could not be reliably parsed from the page's text layout (no delimiter between one item's trailing description and the next item's name in a few spots) and were left blank rather than guessed; every dish name and price was verified directly against its position relative to the '$' price marker in the source, independent of that issue.
